economic_variable: Three-month Treasury-bill rate level (TB) as ICAPM state variable
exact_quotation: The data on the FFR and the 3-month TB rate are from the St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank.
frequency_stated_by_authors: not stated; monthly is implied by the monthly asset-pricing design
sample: article_pdf:p.935 states the sample period is Jan. 1972-Dec. 2013
unresolved_ambiguity: The authors write 3-month TB rate without distinguishing the secondary-market rate from the auction-based or constant-maturity rate, and give no series code, vintage, or daily-to-monthly aggregation rule. TB3MS is a documented reconstruction of this concept, not a verified exact input. No daily series is named anywhere in the article or supplement.

economic_variable: Federal funds rate innovation (FFR-tilde) baseline hedging factor
exact_quotation: the innovations in both ICAPM state variables are obtained from the following AR(1) processes: FFR_{t+1} = 0.000 + 0.991 FFR_t, R2 = 0.98, (0.99) (147.26)
source_named_by_authors: derived from the St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank federal funds rate
units_stated_by_authors: reported in percent in Table 1; the article does not state whether this is an annualized rate percentage point or a monthly percent
estimator: OLS with reported t-ratios in parentheses
unresolved_ambiguity: The article does not state the first regression pair. If the AR(1) is estimated on regressor months 1972:01-2013:11 the innovation exists only for 1972:02-2013:12 (503 months); if the rate level is drawn from 1971:12 the innovation covers all 504 baseline months. The article also does not state whether the AR(1) coefficients are rounded for display or are the estimates actually used to form the residual.

economic_variable: Treasury-bill rate innovation (TB-tilde) alternative hedging factor
source_named_by_authors: derived from the St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank 3-month Treasury-bill rate
units_stated_by_authors: reported in percent in Table 1; the article does not state whether this is an annualized rate percentage point or a monthly percent
estimator: OLS with reported t-ratios in parentheses
unresolved_ambiguity: Same first-regression-pair ambiguity as RATE_EV_03. The article says and similarly for TB rather than writing the residual definition out.

economic_variable: Explicit residual definition for the baseline innovation
exact_quotation: The innovation in the FFR is given by FFR-tilde_{t+1} = FFR_{t+1} - 0.000 - 0.991 FFR_t and similarly for TB.
quotation_location: article_pdf:p.935:Section III.B Data:sentence following the AR equations
transformation: residual of the AR(1) with intercept
unresolved_ambiguity: The displayed formula uses the rounded coefficients 0.000 and 0.991. The article does not say whether the empirical factor was built from rounded or unrounded coefficients; the two differ materially for a coefficient reported to three decimals against a rate level that reaches 19 percent.

economic_variable: Timing of the innovation in the first-pass regression
exact_quotation: R_{i,t+1} - R_{f,t+1} = delta_i + beta_{i,M} RM_{t+1} + beta_{i,FFR} FFR-tilde_{t+1} + epsilon_{i,t+1}
units_stated_by_authors: excess returns in percent per month
transformation: contemporaneous same-month alignment of the return and the innovation
estimator: OLS time-series multiple regression per test asset
unresolved_ambiguity: The equation fixes contemporaneous alignment unambiguously. It does not state the residual covariance estimator or Newey-West lag rule for the first pass.

economic_variable: Alternative first-difference rate factors (appendix robustness only)
exact_quotation: Following Hahn and Lee (2006) and Maio and Santa-Clara (2012), the innovation in the Fed funds rate corresponds to the first-difference in this variable, FFR-tilde_{t+1} = FFR_{t+1} - FFR_t, and similarly for TB.
source_named_by_authors: derived from the same St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank rate levels
transformation: first difference of the rate level
unresolved_ambiguity: This is an explicitly labelled robustness alternative and does not redefine the baseline. No separate source or vintage is given.
